title: Ind AS 111 "Joint Arrangements"
outcomes: Classify joint arrangements as joint operations or joint ventures.
Account for interests in joint operations.
Account for interests in joint ventures and by non-controlling parties.

meta.exam_tip: Use the decision steps: separate vehicle? legal form? contract? other facts?

concepts.title: Identifying joint control
body: Ind AS 111 applies to all entities that are parties to a joint arrangement. A joint arrangement has two features: the parties are bound by a contractual arrangement, and that arrangement gives two or more of them joint control.

To test joint control: first, does the contract give all the parties, or a group of them, collective control? Then, do decisions about relevant activities require the unanimous consent of the parties that collectively control it?
An arrangement can be joint even if not all parties have joint control. A party with a casting vote or the ability to decide alone has control, not joint control.
concepts.work: Three parties with 50:30:20 and a rule needing 75% approval: the 50 and 30 share joint control only if they are the only combination that can reach 75%.

concepts.title: Classifying: joint operation or joint venture
body: Classification depends on rights and obligations. In a joint operation, each party owns its share of the assets and owes its share of the debts. A joint venture: parties have rights to the net assets.

If no separate vehicle is used, the arrangement is automatically a joint operation. If structured through a separate vehicle, consider: the legal form of the vehicle (does it confer rights to assets and obligations to parties?); the contractual terms; and other facts and circumstances (e.g. parties take substantially all output and are the only source of cash, meaning they effectively fund liabilities).
Classification is reassessed when facts and circumstances change.
concepts.analogy: No vehicle → joint operation; vehicle → look through legal form, contract and other facts.
concepts.work: An output-sharing company funded only by its owners is a joint operation.

concepts.title: Accounting by joint operators
body: A joint operator recognises, in relation to its interest: its assets (including its share of jointly held assets), its liabilities (including its share of joint liabilities), its revenue from selling its share of output, its share of revenue from sale of output by the operation, and its expenses including its share of joint expenses.
These are accounted for under the relevant Ind AS — in both separate and consolidated statements.

On sales by the operator to the joint operation, gains are recognised only to the extent of other parties' interests; on purchases from the operation, the operator's share of gains is not recognised until resale to a third party. Acquisition of an interest in a joint operation that is a business applies Ind AS 103 principles.
concepts.analogy: Joint operators book their slices line by line.
concepts.work: A 40% operator books 40% of the shared plant.

concepts.title: Accounting by joint venturers and other parties
body: A joint venturer recognises its interest as an investment and accounts for it using the equity method under Ind AS 28 (unless exempt). In separate statements, it applies Ind AS 27 (cost, Ind AS 109 or equity method).
A participant in a joint operation who lacks joint control accounts like a joint operator if it has rights to assets and obligations for liabilities; otherwise by the relevant Ind AS.
A party to a joint venture without joint control applies Ind AS 109, or Ind AS 28 if it has significant influence.
concepts.analogy: Joint venturers use one line — the equity method.
concepts.work: A 50:50 company with net asset rights is equity-accounted by each owner.

illustrations.title: A joint operation
illustrations.q: Alpha Ltd. and Beta Ltd. share joint control (40:60) of an unincorporated refinery arrangement. Each has rights to its share of the plant and output and is liable for its share of debts. The arrangement's plant is ₹500 crore, liabilities ₹200 crore, revenue ₹300 crore and expenses ₹200 crore. What does Alpha recognise?

jobs.title: Reviewing a JV agreement
jobs.situation: The company signed a 50:50 agreement to set up a manufacturing company.
steps: Confirm joint control from decision rules.
Check whether a separate vehicle exists.
Analyse legal form, contract terms and other facts.
Apply equity method or line-by-line share.
jobs.takeaway: Rights and obligations, not legal form alone, decide classification.

mcqs.q: An arrangement not structured through a separate vehicle is:
mcqs.explain: Parties have direct rights. In practice: line-by-line share.
mcqs.topic: Classifying: joint operation or joint venture

mcqs.q: A joint venturer accounts for its interest using:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 28 applies. In practice: one-line.
mcqs.topic: Accounting by joint venturers and other parties

mcqs.q: A party with a casting vote in a 50:50 company has:
mcqs.explain: It can decide alone. In practice: consolidate.

mcqs.q: Parties taking substantially all output and being the only cash source suggests:
mcqs.explain: Other facts override legal form. In practice: they fund liabilities.
mcqs.topic: Classifying: joint operation or joint venture

options: Its share of assets, liabilities, revenue and expenses
mcqs.explain: Line-by-line in both statements. In practice: own assets too.

mcqs.q: Joint control requires decisions about relevant activities to be:
mcqs.explain: Unanimity is essential. In practice: check agreement.

mcqs.q: A party in a joint venture without joint control but with significant influence applies:
mcqs.explain: Equity method as associate. In practice: else Ind AS 109.
mcqs.topic: Accounting by joint venturers and other parties

mcqs.q: Acquiring an interest in a joint operation that is a business applies:
mcqs.explain: Goodwill may arise. In practice: fair value share of assets.

summary: JO: rights to assets, obligations for liabilities.
JO: line-by-line share; JV: equity method.
remember: Output-sharing vehicles can be joint operations.

viva.q: What are the features of a joint arrangement?
viva.model: Parties are bound by a contractual arrangement that gives two or more of them joint control.

viva.q: How is a joint arrangement classified?
viva.model: By the parties' rights and obligations: rights to assets and obligations for liabilities make it a joint operation; rights to net assets make it a joint venture.

viva.q: Which factors are considered for a separate vehicle?
viva.model: Its legal form, the terms of the contractual arrangement and other facts and circumstances.

viva.q: How does a joint operator account in separate statements?
viva.model: The same as in consolidated statements — recognising its share of assets, liabilities, revenue and expenses.

viva.q: How does a joint venturer account?
viva.model: It recognises an investment and applies the equity method under Ind AS 28.

cases.title: Delta–Echo arrangement
cases.case: Delta Ltd. and Echo Ltd. form Fox Pvt Ltd. (50:50) to make components. All relevant decisions need both parties' approval. Fox sells all output to Delta and Echo at cost, and they pay Fox's debts as needed. Delta sells raw materials to Fox for ₹20 crore at a profit of ₹4 crore; Fox still holds them.

mcqs.explain: Parties take output and fund liabilities. In practice: other facts override legal form.
mcqs.topic: Classifying: joint operation or joint venture

options: Recognising its 50% share of assets, liabilities, income and expenses
mcqs.explain: Joint operator accounting. In practice: both statements.

mcqs.q: Profit Delta recognises on the raw material sale (₹ crore):
mcqs.explain: Only to the extent of Echo's 50% interest. In practice: defer own share.

mcqs.q: If the agreement allowed Delta alone to decide, Fox would be:
mcqs.explain: Sole decision power is control. In practice: consolidate.
